# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which maps light colors to wire colors (purple → green, red → blue, white → yellow) and notes that the light changes every round across a three-color cycle.

However, I can only communicate with Deaf via gestures, and Blind cannot see gestures or colors. Moreover, no convention has been established yet for what any gesture means, and I do not know what Deaf sees on the bomb (such as wire layout or initial light state). Since Deaf can speak to both Blind and me, the directed communication loop flows Blind → Mute → Deaf → Blind. 

Until Deaf sees the bomb and establishes a gesture code, any sign I send would have no agreed meaning. I will wait for Deaf to observe the bomb and define our protocol.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can act by cutting wire 1, 2, or 3. I cannot see gestures, only hear speech. Deaf will see the bomb and speak its details to you. Once you read the manual, gesture the target wire number to Deaf so Deaf can speak it out loud for me to cut.
Deaf says: Bomb state: Display shows 0. Light is white. 3 wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is blue. Mute, check the manual. Since Blind cannot see your gestures, gesture to me what to do: use ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. If there is another action, gesture it clearly.

I have the defusal manual:
- Purple light -> cut Green wire (Wire 2)
- Red light -> cut Blue wire (Wire 3)
- White light -> cut Yellow wire (Wire 1)
Crucially, the manual states: *"The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."*

Deaf reported in Round 1 that the light is White and asked for a gesture (☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or another clear action).
However, Deaf does not have the manual and does not know the light changes every round. If I signal wire 1 now, Deaf will instruct Blind to cut in Round 3, at which point the light will have changed to another color in the cycle, causing a detonation.

We need Deaf to see the light change in Round 2 to establish the color cycle, and prevent Blind from acting prematurely. Deaf explicitly invited: *"If there is another action, gesture it clearly."*
I will gesture ✋ (hold / wait) to Deaf. Deaf will observe the bomb state update in Round 2, report the new light color, and keep Blind from cutting until the timing matches.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Do not cut anything yet. The light turned from white to PURPLE. Display shows 0. Wires are 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. What controls do you feel, and did you touch or hold anything? Mute: You gestured ✋. Please clarify your command using this exact code on your next turn: ✋ = HOLD button, 👆 = PRESS/RELEASE button, ☝ = CUT wire 1 (yellow), ✌ = CUT wire 2 (green), 🤟 = CUT wire 3 (blue), 👌 = WAIT/do nothing. If a number is needed for when to act, show: 👌=0, ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5.

I will signal Deaf to have Blind cut wire 1 (yellow).

The manual requires:
- Purple -> cut green (Wire 2)
- Red -> cut blue (Wire 3)
- White -> cut yellow (Wire 1)

The light sequence is White (Round 1) -> Purple (Round 2) -> Red (Round 3) -> White (Round 4).
Deaf will receive this gesture in Round 3 and instruct Blind to cut. Blind will execute the cut on Round 4, when the light returns to White. Under Deaf's code, ☝ designates cutting Wire 1 (yellow).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not touched anything. In my interface, there are no buttons to press or hold—my only possible action is act(op='cut', position=N) where N is wire 1, 2, or 3. The light is now purple, display is 0, wires are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Please use the gesture code Deaf just gave you to indicate which of the three wires (1, 2, or 3) I must cut.
Deaf says: Blind: Display is 0, light is currently RED. Wires are 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Mute just gestured ☝. If you are not holding a button, Mute's signal means CUT WIRE 1 (yellow). If you are currently holding a button, Mute's signal is 1 (release on 1 / according to manual rule for 1).

The manual specifies:
- Purple light → cut Green wire (wire 2)
- Red light → cut Blue wire (wire 3)
- White light → cut Yellow wire (wire 1)

The light cycle has been:
- Round 1: White
- Round 2: Purple
- Round 3: Red
- Round 4: White

At the end of Round 3, Deaf instructed Blind to cut Wire 1 (Yellow). Blind receives this instruction at the start of Round 4 and will execute the cut during their turn in Round 4, precisely when the light is White. Yellow wire cut on White light is the correct defusal action.

No further action or gesture is needed from me this round.

```
wait()
```
